notes: Identity verified from the supplied canonical text: Research Article; title Specks of Dirt and Tons of Pain: Dosage Distinguishes Impurity From Harm; Joshua Rottman and Liane Young; Psychological Science 2019, Vol. 30(8), 1151–1160; DOI 10.1177/0956797619855382. The cache contains the primary report with methods, results, discussion and references, not merely an abstract or secondary account. No PDF was supplied. N = 177 is the explicitly stated final Study 1 participant sample after 12 attention-check exclusions and 12 duplicate-pilot-worker-ID exclusions. These participants supplied the repeated moral judgments analyzed by the Study 1 mixed model, with participant and scenario random intercepts. N denotes participant clusters, not the number of judgment observations or scenarios; no observation total or N from degrees of freedom is inferred. Both domain and dosage vary within participants. No sample arithmetic was needed. Only assigned unfinished fields were populated; all unassigned fields and the replication side are placeholders.
